subject: Post-demo recap & benchmarking scope for Strata Labs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.co@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@stratalabs.ai>, Victor Ramos <victor@stratalabs.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & initial benchmarking scope

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation and clear signal on what matters for Strata Labs. Short recap and proposed next steps so we can line up an apples-to-apples evaluation against the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

Recap (what we heard)
- Production target: ~10k inference requests/day, burstable to ~50k/day for peak jobs.
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile under 300ms for text-completion workloads at median seq len ~120 tokens.
- Quality bar: hallucination tolerance is low for retrieval-augmented workflows; you need measurable regression checks vs your current baseline.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence + audit log exports required for procurement.

Proposed benchmark scope (high level)
1) Model quality (P0): 300 labeled prompts for hallucination detection and factual accuracy (we'll provide the labeling rubric).
2) Regression checks: run our perturbation suite (see attached benchmark_prompts_v1.csv) to compare current HyperscalerX baseline vs Redwood variants.
3) End-to-end perf: 1-hour steady-state at target qps, and a 30-minute burst test. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and cold-start behavior.
4) Cost and token accounting: per-token costs with identical request mix + batching/caching profiles.

Immediate asks from us
- Share a service account or API key for Strata staging so we can run side-by-side tests (HyperscalerX + Redwood dedicated/private instance).
- Confirm whether the 300 labeled prompts can be shared publicly or if they must use your private dataset (affects how we run labeling).
- Target window: Wed 3/22 or Thu 3/23 for the first runs (2-hour block each day).

Owners & timeline
- Marissa (me): run quality/regression suite and own deliverables 
- Ben: infra provisioning for a dedicated test instance and logging hooks
- Aditya: security and SOC2 evidence handoff

Attachments: Strata_PostDemo_SLA_Questions.pdf (procurement questions), benchmark_prompts_v1.csv (starter prompt set).

Next: if that scope looks right, I suggest locking Wed 3/22 9–11am PT for the first head-to-head. I can turn around the detailed runbook today if you confirm.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and aligned with what Victor and I discussed internally. A few clarifications and resources from our side: 

- We can provision a staging API key for Redwood to hit our staging dataset; we will create a scoped service account limited to the test bucket. I'll send the invite separately (security requires an allowlist of IPs).
- The 300 labeled prompts: we prefer to keep them private (contain customer PII). We can instead provide a synthetic, PII-free shard of 200 prompts for public testing and make the full set available for on-prem or in our VPC run.
- SOC2: vendor attestation is sufficient for the procurement phase; we will still request the audit log export capability for final signoff.

Requests for Redwood team before Wed 3/22 run:
- Can you confirm how your KV/prefix caching behaves across parallel requests? We need to know expected hit-rate assumptions if we mimic our retrieval cache in the test.
- Can you document the batching strategy you plan to use for the steady-state run (max batch size, batching window)?

Also: Victor asked if Redwood can do a paired A/B run against HyperscalerX in the same time window (we will enable both keys). He wants throughput-limited tests rather than latency-only, to see cost per useful token under realistic batching.

We'll aim to get the service account to you by EOD.

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Head of ML Engineering | Strata Labs

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & initial benchmarking scope

Appreciate the quick reply and the constraints — we'll adapt. Below is the concrete runbook I'll execute once we have the staging credentials + allowlist. If anything needs to be changed, flag it and we'll update the runbook before Wed.

Bench runbook (detailed)
A) Quality & hallucination suite (isolated, offline)- Dataset: Strata private 300-sample set (or synthetic 200-shard if private not available).- Metric: Hallucination rate = (# responses with at least one unsupported factual assertion) / (total labeled responses). Labeling is binary per response.- Output: confusion matrix vs your baseline answers + sample-level tags for review.

B) Regression & prompt perturbation (online sampling)- Perturbations: paraphrase prompts, remove context, add noisy retrieved docs.- Runs: baseline (HyperscalerX), Redwood quantized (8-bit), Redwood standard fp16.- Metric: semantic similarity (embedding + threshold), factual precision on retrieval prompts, and hallucination delta vs baseline.

C) Perf & cost (live)- Test windows: 9:00–10:00 PT = steady-state @ target qps; 10:30–11:00 PT = 30-min burst.- Batching config: we'll start with max_batch_size=64 and batching_window=20ms, then sweep to {32, 128} and {10ms, 50ms} respectively. Documenting results for each combo.- Measuring: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, worker utilization, and per-token cost computed from your and our cloud billing export.

D) Deliverables & timing- Within 24 hours: raw run logs + perf dashboards snapshot.- Within 3 business days: cleaned comparison report with hallucination-rate tables, example failure cases, and recommended config to meet p99 SLOs while minimizing cost.

E) Security & procurement handoff- Aditya will compile SOC2 attestation and a snippet about audit log exports.

Couple of engineering notes in response to your questions: 
- KV/prefix caching: our runtime supports request-level prefix caching and a shared KV cache per model instance. Hit rate will depend on how often retrieval prefixes repeat; for retrieval-augmented tests we can instrument cache hit/miss and include that in the logs.- Batching strategy: continuous batching with adaptive windowing — we'll start with the explicit sweep above and note the affect on p99.

If you confirm Wed 3/22 9–11am PT, Ben will provision the dedicated infra and I will kick off the runs. Also, please send the service account + allowlist details (we'll provide our test IP ranges).

Thanks,
Marissa
